    Getting Started

    intro.Rmd

    This vignette shows the smallest useful tsflow workflow:

    • define a pipeline in YAML
    • plan it
    • inspect the dependency DAG
    • execute it with injected inputs

    Define A Pipeline

    Start with a small YAML pipeline that uses one raw input and two derived series.

    library(tsflow)

pipeline_path <- tempfile(fileext = ".yml")

writeLines(
    c(
        "vars:",
        "  factor: 100",
        "outputs:",
        "  - growth_index",
        "series:",
        "  - name: raw_a",
        "    source:",
        "      type: injected",
        "  - name: scaled_a",
        "    steps:",
        "      - input: raw_a",
        "      - call:",
        "          name: scale",
        "          kwargs:",
        "            factor:",
        "              var: factor",
        "  - name: growth_index",
        "    steps:",
        "      - input: scaled_a",
        "      - call:",
        "          name: add_constant",
        "          args:",
        "            - 5"
    ),
    con = pipeline_path
)

cat(paste(readLines(pipeline_path), collapse = "\n"))
#> vars:
#>   factor: 100
#> outputs:
#>   - growth_index
#> series:
#>   - name: raw_a
#>     source:
#>       type: injected
#>   - name: scaled_a
#>     steps:
#>       - input: raw_a
#>       - call:
#>           name: scale
#>           kwargs:
#>             factor:
#>               var: factor
#>   - name: growth_index
#>     steps:
#>       - input: scaled_a
#>       - call:
#>           name: add_constant
#>           args:
#>             - 5

    Define Transforms

    Transforms are ordinary R functions. tsflow resolves bare transform names from the transform_env that you pass to planning and execution.

    scale <- function(x, factor) {
    x * factor
}

add_constant <- function(x, value) {
    x + value
}

    Plan The Pipeline

    Planning reads the file, validates it, and builds a dependency DAG.

    plan <- plan_pipeline(
    path = pipeline_path,
    transform_env = environment()
)

plan
#> <PipelinePlan>
#>   nodes: 3
#>   outputs: 1
#>   execution order: 3
#>   output names: growth_index
plan$dag$order
#> [1] "raw_a"        "scaled_a"     "growth_index"
dag_edges(plan$dag)
#>       from           to
#> 1    raw_a     scaled_a
#> 2 scaled_a growth_index

    If igraph and visNetwork are installed, you can inspect the DAG as an interactive HTML widget.

    dag_to_visnetwork(plan)
    Click a node to inspect the upstream calculation path.

    The widget is useful for understanding dependency structure before you run the pipeline. Hovering a node shows the ordered pipe that produces it.

    Advanced Debugging: Inspect A Cycle

    build_dag() is strict by default and fails when the dependency graph is not acyclic.

    cyclic_spec <- normalize_pipeline(list(
    series = list(
        list(
            name = "series_a",
            steps = list(
                list(input = "series_b")
            )
        ),
        list(
            name = "series_b",
            steps = list(
                list(input = "series_a")
            )
        )
    )
))

try(build_dag(cyclic_spec))
#> Error : dependency graph contains a cycle involving: series_a, series_b

    For debugging, you can opt in to retaining the graph, inspect the involved nodes, and render just that problematic subgraph.

    cyclic_dag <- build_dag(cyclic_spec, allow_cycles = TRUE)

cyclic_dag$cycle_nodes
#> [1] "series_a" "series_b"
dag_subgraph(cyclic_dag, nodes = cyclic_dag$cycle_nodes)
#> $nodes
#> [1] "series_a" "series_b"
#> 
#> $edges
#>       from       to label
#> 1 series_b series_a input
#> 2 series_a series_b input
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "DAGSubgraph" "tsflow_spec"
    dag_to_visnetwork(cyclic_dag, nodes = cyclic_dag$cycle_nodes)
    Click a node to inspect the upstream calculation path.

    This keeps cycle detection explicit while still giving you a visual debugging path when a specification needs to be untangled.

    Execute The Pipeline

    Raw inputs are injected at runtime as named ts objects.

    inputs <- list(
    raw_a = stats::ts(c(1, 2, 3, 4), start = c(2020, 1), frequency = 4)
)

result <- execute_pipeline(
    path = pipeline_path,
    inputs = inputs,
    transform_env = environment()
)

result$outputs$growth_index
#>      Qtr1 Qtr2 Qtr3 Qtr4
#> 2020  105  205  305  405

    You can also inspect the full executed state:

    names(result$values)
#> [1] "raw_a"        "scaled_a"     "growth_index"
result$values$scaled_a
#>      Qtr1 Qtr2 Qtr3 Qtr4
#> 2020  100  200  300  400
result$values$growth_index
#>      Qtr1 Qtr2 Qtr3 Qtr4
#> 2020  105  205  305  405

    Advanced Debugging: Step Into One Node

    Sometimes a series is still too coarse as one DAG node and you want to inspect its calculation step by step. expand_node_dag() builds a small debugging view for one selected node.

    expanded <- expand_node_dag(plan, "growth_index")

expanded$nodes
#> [1] "scaled_a"             "growth_index::step_1" "growth_index"
expanded$edges
#>                   from                   to  label
#> 1             scaled_a growth_index::step_1  input
#> 2 growth_index::step_1         growth_index output

    If igraph and visNetwork are installed, you can render that expanded node graph directly:

    dag_to_visnetwork(expanded)
    Click a node to inspect the upstream calculation path.

    This keeps the main DAG compact while still letting you inspect the ordered pipe inside one node when you need to debug or explain a calculation.

    Advanced Debugging: Inspect A Failed Node Step By Step

    You can also replay the internal steps of one node against an executed result. This is useful when a series failed and you want to see which internal step failed and which later steps were never reached.

    explode <- function(x) {
    stop("kaboom", call. = FALSE)
}

failing_path <- tempfile(fileext = ".yml")

writeLines(
    c(
        "series:",
        "  - name: raw_b",
        "    source:",
        "      type: injected",
        "  - name: broken_series",
        "    steps:",
        "      - input: raw_b",
        "      - call:",
        "          name: scale",
        "          args:",
        "            - 10",
        "      - call:",
        "          name: explode",
        "      - call:",
        "          name: add_constant",
        "          args:",
        "            - 5"
    ),
    con = failing_path
)

failed_result <- suppressWarnings(execute_pipeline(
    path = failing_path,
    inputs = list(raw_b = stats::ts(c(1, 2, 3, 4), start = c(2020, 1), frequency = 4)),
    transform_env = environment(),
    error_mode = "collect",
    progress = FALSE
))

expanded_failed <- expand_node_result(
    failed_result,
    "broken_series",
    transform_env = environment()
)

expanded_failed$failed_step
#> [1] "broken_series::step_2"
expanded_failed$errors
#> $`broken_series::step_2`
#> [1] "\033[1m\033[22mtransform `explode` failed: kaboom"
#> 
#> $broken_series
#> [1] "node replay stopped at `broken_series::step_2`"
expanded_failed$dag$node_status
#>                 raw_b broken_series::step_1 broken_series::step_2 
#>                  "ok"                  "ok"              "failed" 
#> broken_series::step_3         broken_series 
#>             "skipped"             "skipped"
expanded_failed$values
#> $raw_b
#>      Qtr1 Qtr2 Qtr3 Qtr4
#> 2020    1    2    3    4
#> 
#> $`broken_series::step_1`
#>      Qtr1 Qtr2 Qtr3 Qtr4
#> 2020   10   20   30   40

    The failed replay still captures the value of the successful internal step, and marks the failed step plus downstream internal steps in the expanded graph.

    dag_to_visnetwork(expanded_failed)
    Click a node to inspect the upstream calculation path.

    Next Steps

    After the basic YAML workflow works, the next useful patterns are:

    • use CSV plus a sibling sidecar YAML file for spreadsheet-style authoring
    • save compiled YAML with write_pipeline()
    • inspect focused DAG subgraphs with dag_to_visnetwork()
    • step into one node with expand_node_dag()
